newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian politician shot dead, associates say.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian politician shot dead, associates say.

text.p: A wealthy Nigerian politician and businesswoman was shot dead in her home in the southwestern city of Ibadan on Thursday, her associates said.

They said Suliat Adedeji, a member of the advisory committee of the National Centre Party of Nigeria, was attacked by four unknown assailants who broke into her house after overpowering watchmen there.
"She was having breakfast and I understand they demanded 50 million naira ($625,000) and she said they must be joking but they shot her instead," said a member of her party in Lagos.
"She died while she was being rushed to hospital," he added.

Adedeji was a member of the National Party of Nigeria which won the 1979 presidential election. The military seized power four years later and in 1993 she contested a presidential election which was widely believed to have been won by businessman Moshood Abiola but was annulled by the military.
Adedeji's killing was the third murder of its kind in southwestern Nigeria in the past five months months.
In June Abiola's senior wife was shot while in traffic in Lagos. Her murder was followed by that of an 80-year-old industrialist, Madam Bisoye Tejuosho, who was hacked to death in her home.
None of the murders have been solved.
